analysis.title: Frontdoor Inc. (FTDR) 3Q26 Earnings Recap: Mid-Single-Digit Revenue Growth, Cost Savings, and Efficiencies Offset Slowdown in Housing, Though Upside is Captured in Valuation
key_insights: GS maintains a Neutral rating on FTDR and raises the 12-month price target to $93 from $81. The stock closed at $95.98 on 5 Nov 2026, which implies 3.1% downside. GS says much of the upside is already reflected in the valuation.

All three warranty channels contributed to a 1% increase in member count in 3Q26, and the company guides to a similar rate of growth for the full year. Renewal and direct-to-consumer outlooks improved and offset pressure in the real estate channel.

The retention rate rose 30bps YOY to 79.7%, supported by app engagement, about 84% preferred-contractor penetration and about 85% auto-pay adoption. Discounted cohorts continue to renew at a higher rate than non-promotional members, and GS sees improving unit economics.

Real estate channel membership rose 5%, with a capture rate of 5+% of 3Q existing home sales. FTDR now expects the full-year real estate member count to be flat, as mortgage rates in the 7% range and weaker consumer confidence weigh on housing turnover. GS believes the company can accelerate if conditions improve.

The HVAC upgrade business is expected to grow 37% this year to about $175mn. GS forecasts the other segment at $239mn in 2026 (+23.6% YOY) against the $235-240mn guide, and +14.2% in 2027 as the nationwide appliances launch completes in 2027. Growth is expected to moderate off tough multi-year comps.

Gross margin pricing, cost controls and supply chain efforts partly offset a $9mn weather headwind, negative mix shift and inflation. Inflation is tracking low-single-digit growth this year against about 4% price realization. State-level HVAC pricing aligns prices with regional costs.

HVAC carries a targeted gross margin of about 20%, against GS's 2027 consolidated gross margin estimate of 53.9%. GS notes limited incremental SG&A, which supports the long-term mid-20% EBITDA margin target. GS models 2026 adj. EBITDA margin at 27.0% (up 60bps YOY, in line with guide) and 72bps of contraction in 2027.

Management described digital capabilities across the member journey and a defined process for handling cancellation requests regardless of origin. The company sees consumer AI agents as a possible incremental channel for brand awareness and engagement, though adoption is early.

GS expects inflation to rise in 2027 as suppliers pass through higher commodity prices, including energy. GS is confident FTDR can balance trade service fees and member pricing to deliver mid-single-digit revenue growth over the next several years.

GS models free cash flow of $367mn in 2026 and $417mn in 2027, supporting a lower share count and growth investments. GS sees a path to the $2.5bn 2028 revenue target, with upside to the mid-20% adj. EBITDA margin target.

Estimate changes: 2026 adj. EPS to $4.85 from $4.75, 2027 to $5.30 from $5.20, 2028 to $6.00 from $5.70. 2026 revenue estimate rises to $2,213mn from $2,197mn. The price target rests on 11.8x (from 11.0x) Q5-Q8 adj. EBITDA, with the higher multiple reflecting confidence in strategic initiatives.
Scenario analysis: the 12-month upside case is $118 (20.0x 2027 EPS) and the downside case is $66 (14.0x 2027 EPS). GS sees balanced risk/reward at the current valuation.

market_movers.rationale: Price target raised to $93 from $81 on a higher 11.8x multiple of Q5-Q8 adj. EBITDA and higher estimates after the 3Q26 print. Neutral maintained because GS sees much of the upside already in the valuation.

earnings_insights: FTDR 3Q26 (reported 6 Nov 2026 per GS recap): member count grew 1% with all three channels contributing. Retention rose 30bps YOY to 79.7%. Real estate membership rose 5%. Gross margin absorbed a $9mn weather headwind.
GS forecasts 2026 adj. EBITDA margin of 27.0% (up 60bps YOY, in line with company guide) and 72bps of contraction in 2027. GS 2026 EBITDA estimate is $597.8mn on its adjusted basis.
GS forecasts other segment sales of $239mn in 2026 (+23.6% YOY) against company guidance of $235-240mn. HVAC upgrade business is expected by the company to grow 37% this year to about $175mn.
Company now expects flat full-year real estate channel member count, and similar full-year total member count growth of about 1%.
GS next-quarter EPS estimates: 4Q26E $0.38, 1Q27E $0.80, 2Q27E $2.06. 3Q26 EPS shown as $1.81 in the GS forecast table.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Elevated mortgage rates and lower consumer confidence weigh on housing turnover and led FTDR to guide its real estate member count flat for the full year.

macro_indicators.reading: low-single-digit growth in 2026 vs about 4% price realization
macro_indicators.interpretation: GS expects inflation to rise in 2027 as suppliers pass through higher commodity prices, including energy, which could pressure margins if pricing does not keep pace.

risk_factors: Housing turnover moderation and mortgage rates in the 7% range limiting real estate channel growth.
Production shortages or loss of a key supplier.
Greater competition if peers seek to gain share.
Higher raw material costs, including energy, and inability to pass them through to members.
HVAC mix shift toward a roughly 20% gross margin business diluting consolidated gross margin.

tension_points.bull_case: Retention up 30bps to 79.7%, all channels adding members, about 85% auto-pay and 84% preferred-contractor penetration, HVAC and appliances cross-sell, and $367mn of 2026 FCF funding buybacks. GS's upside case is $118 (20.0x 2027 EPS).
tension_points.bear_case: Housing turnover is slowing with mortgage rates in the 7% range, the real estate member count is guided flat, HVAC mix dilutes gross margin and GS models 72bps of EBITDA margin contraction in 2027. The stock at $95.98 sits above the $93 target, and the downside case is $66 (14.0x 2027 EPS).
tension_points.what_invalidates: Inflation rising in 2027 as suppliers pass through higher commodity and energy costs, outpacing the roughly 4% price realization, would undercut the margin leg of the bull case.
